# An integral symmetric-group lattice generated by minimal octahedra in two-subset Kneser independence complexes

## Finding
For each integer \(n\geq4\), let \(G_n\) be the Kneser graph whose vertices are the two-element subsets of \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with adjacency meaning disjointness, and let \(K_n=\operatorname{Ind}(G_n)\). Write \(E_n=\mathbb Z^n\), with coordinate basis \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\), and let \(V_n=\ker(\varepsilon:E_n\to\mathbb Z)\), where \(\varepsilon(e_i)=1\). The coordinate-permutation action of \(S_n\) on second integral homology admits a natural integral identification
\[
H_2(K_n;\mathbb Z)\cong\bigwedge^3 V_n.
\]
In particular it is torsion-free of rank \(\binom{n-1}{3}\), and over \(\mathbb Q\) it is the irreducible hook Specht representation \(S^{(n-3,1,1,1)}\).

For each four-subset \(Q\subseteq[n]\), the six Kneser vertices indexed by two-subsets of \(Q\) induce the octahedral two-sphere \((S^0)^{*3}\). Orient its fundamental cycle \(q_Q\) as in the proof below. The \(\binom n4\) integral classes \([q_Q]\) generate all of \(H_2(K_n;\mathbb Z)\). Every such class is primitive; the \(\binom{n-1}3\) cycles with \(1\in Q\) form an integral basis. All integral relations between these natural generators are generated by the five-term relations
\[
\sum_{r=1}^5(-1)^{r-1}[q_{S\setminus\{s_r\}}]=0,
\quad S=\{s_1<\cdots<s_5\}\subseteq[n].
\]
Six is the minimum possible number of Kneser vertices supporting a nonzero second-homology class, so this is an integral generating family consisting entirely of minimum-support spheres.

The integral representation determines the complete rational character. If a permutation \(\sigma\in S_n\) has cycle lengths \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\), then
\[
\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\sigma\mid H_2(K_n;\mathbb Q)\bigr)
=[t^3]\,\frac{\prod_{j=1}^r(1-(-t)^{\ell_j})}{1+t}.
\]

## Assumptions and scope
The graph is the ordinary disjointness Kneser graph on the complete family of two-subsets, not the stable Kneser graph or the Lovász neighborhood complex. Homology is unreduced in degree two, with integral coefficients. The claim applies to every integer \(n\geq4\), with the natural action of all permutations of the underlying \(n\) labels. A homology support means a subset of vertices of this Kneser graph (that is, a family of two-subsets of \([n]\)); the minimum of six is not a minimum on ground-set labels. The explicit five-term relations concern homology classes, not necessarily equality of the chosen simplicial chains.

## Proof
**1. An equivariant subcomplex.** Every independent family of two-subsets consists of pairwise intersecting edges of the complete graph on \([n]\). A family of at least four distinct edges with this property has a common endpoint: indeed, three edges with no common endpoint must be the triangle on three ground labels, and no fourth distinct edge can meet all three. Hence the maximal faces of \(K_n\) are the star simplices \(A_i\), consisting of all pairs containing \(i\), and the exceptional triangular faces \(T_{ijk}\), with vertices \(\{i,j\},\{i,k\},\{j,k\}\), for \(i<j<k\).

Let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\). Distinct star simplices meet in exactly one Kneser vertex \(\{i,j\}\); no three star simplices have a common vertex. Each star and each nonempty pairwise intersection is contractible. The Mayer–Vietoris complex of this permutation-invariant cover therefore identifies, naturally and \(S_n\)-equivariantly, \(H_1(U;\mathbb Z)\) with the integral cycle space of the complete graph on the ground labels. Concretely, writing \(\partial_2=\iota_\varepsilon:\bigwedge^2 E_n\to E_n\), this cycle space is \(\ker\partial_2=\bigwedge^2 V_n\). Also \(H_2(U;\mathbb Z)=0\) and \(U\) is connected.

**2. The relative connecting map.** The only simplices of \(K_n\) not in \(U\) are the interiors of the exceptional triangular faces \(T_{ijk}\). Orient \(T_{ijk}\) by ordering its Kneser vertices \([\{j,k\},\{i,k\},\{i,j\}]\). With this complementary-edge orientation, the relative group \(C_2(K_n,U;\mathbb Z)\) is the signed triple-permutation module \(\bigwedge^3 E_n\); all other relative groups vanish. The connecting map in the long exact sequence of the pair sends the triangle \(T_{ijk}\) to the oriented three-cycle on \(i,j,k\) in the complete-graph nerve. Thus, up to an immaterial uniform global orientation sign, it is the standard contraction
\[
\partial_3=\iota_\varepsilon:\bigwedge^3E_n\longrightarrow\ker(\partial_2)\subseteq\bigwedge^2E_n,
\quad
\partial_3(e_i\wedge e_j\wedge e_k)
=e_j\wedge e_k-e_i\wedge e_k+e_i\wedge e_j.
\]
This is a statement about the integral chain map, not just its rational rank. The long exact sequence now gives the natural \(S_n\)-equivariant identification
\[
H_2(K_n;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\ker(\partial_3)=\bigwedge^3 V_n.
\]
The last equality follows integrally from the split short exact sequence \(0\to V_n\to E_n\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\mathbb Z\to0\): take the basis \(e_1,e_2-e_1,\ldots,e_n-e_1\) and evaluate \(\iota_\varepsilon\). It also shows surjectivity of \(\partial_3\), hence \(H_1(K_n;\mathbb Z)=0\).

**3. Minimal octahedra, integral generation and relations.** For \(Q=\{a<b<c<d\}\), the six edges of its induced \(K_4\) comprise exactly three complementary opposite pairs
\[
(\{a,b\},\{c,d\}),\qquad(\{a,c\},\{b,d\}),\qquad(\{a,d\},\{b,c\}).
\]
A face contains at most one from each opposite pair, so this induced complex is the boundary of the three-dimensional cross-polytope. Orient its eight facets by selecting one edge from each displayed opposite pair, in the displayed pair order, with coefficient \((-1)^m\) if \(m\) second choices are made. Orient \(q_Q\) globally so that its relative image in \(\bigwedge^3E_n\) is
\[
\partial_4(e_a\wedge e_b\wedge e_c\wedge e_d)
=e_b\wedge e_c\wedge e_d-e_a\wedge e_c\wedge e_d
+e_a\wedge e_b\wedge e_d-e_a\wedge e_b\wedge e_c.
\]
This sign normalization can be checked on the four exceptional triangles in the octahedral boundary, and is compatible with permutations because the orientations of the exceptional triangles use complementary edges. The augmented exterior boundary complex of the \((n-1)\)-simplex is split exact over \(\mathbb Z\). Hence \(\ker\partial_3=\operatorname{im}\partial_4\), and \(\ker\partial_4=\operatorname{im}\partial_5\). This proves integral generation by the \(q_Q\) and proves that the displayed five-term relations generate **all** their integral relations. In the basis of \(V_n\) given by \(e_i-e_1\), the elements \(\partial_4(e_1\wedge e_i\wedge e_j\wedge e_k)\), for \(2\le i<j<k\le n\), are a basis of \(\bigwedge^3V_n\) up to sign. In particular all \(q_Q\) are primitive, using permutation transitivity.

**4. Sharp support.** Each \(K_n\) is a flag complex. Suppose a nonzero second-homology class could be represented on at most five Kneser vertices, and choose such a representative two-cycle with the minimum number of supported vertices \(W\), so \(|W|\le5\). At a supported vertex \(v\), its simplicial link within \(K_n[W]\) is a one-cycle on the neighbors of \(v\) in \(W\). If \(v\) has at most three such neighbors, this link cycle is a boundary in the induced link: every flag complex on at most three vertices has trivial first homology. Coning an integral link filling to \(v\) then removes all triangles incident to \(v\) without introducing any vertices outside \(W\), contradicting minimality. Thus each vertex in \(W\) has at least four neighbors in \(W\). Necessarily \(|W|=5\), and every pair of vertices is adjacent. Flagness now makes \(K_n[W]\) a full four-simplex, with zero second homology, a contradiction. Consequently every nonzero second-homology class has support of at least six vertices; the \(q_Q\) attain the bound.

**5. Character.** Since \(E_n\cong V_n\oplus\mathbb Z\) as rational representations, \(\det(1+t\sigma\mid V_n)=\det(1+t\sigma\mid E_n)/(1+t)\). Each cycle of length \(\ell\) in the coordinate permutation has determinant factor \(1-(-t)^\ell\). The coefficient of \(t^3\) is the trace on \(\bigwedge^3V_n\), proving the character formula. Standard characteristic-zero representation theory identifies this exterior cube with the hook Specht representation of shape \((n-3,1,1,1)\).

## Verification
The included standard-library script `verify_kneser.py` independently enumerates the simplicial face sets for \(4\le n\le8\), their signed boundary matrices, and all four-ground-label octahedral cycles. It checks that each octahedral chain is closed, that relative triangle coefficients agree up to uniform orientation with \(\partial_4\), that every five-term relation vanishes in the relative cycle coordinates, and that the signed action of a transposition and an \(n\)-cycle agrees with the predicted exterior action. It also compares ranks of second boundaries, third boundaries, and octahedral generators over \(\mathbb F_{101}\), obtaining ranks \(1,4,10,20,35\), respectively. These finite tests are consistency checks; the proof of the integral assertions for all \(n\) is the chain-exactness argument above.

To replay from the present directory, run `python3 verify_kneser.py`. The captured output is `verification_output.txt`.

## Relationship to prior work
Barmak's Theorem 4.11 (arXiv:1007.0418, first posted 2 July 2010) already proves the nonequivariant homotopy equivalence \(K_n\simeq\bigvee^{\binom{n-1}{3}}S^2\) and describes the star/exceptional-triangle decomposition. Neither that known homotopy type nor its Betti number is claimed as new here. The additional result is the canonical **integral \(S_n\)-lattice**, including the action of odd permutations, the exact all-symmetry character, primitive minimum-support octahedral generators and their complete five-term relation module. Braun's older work concerns stable Kneser graphs, which have different vertex sets and complexes. Feng and Wang's work on larger-subset Kneser independence complexes explicitly cites Barmak for the two-subset case, but addresses general cross-polytope lower bounds and higher-subset homology. Feng's 2026 rational-homology classification concerns families of three-subsets, not this integral two-subset action.

## Limitations
The result does not classify every six-vertex support of a nonzero class, only constructs a complete symmetry orbit of minimum-support primitive generators. It does not assert an \(S_n\)-equivariant wedge decomposition, which would be stronger than a homology-module isomorphism. The standard chain isomorphism depends on an overall harmless orientation choice. The literature search cannot exclude equivalent work that is not indexed, especially a representation-theoretic reformulation of Barmak's construction. Finite computations alone would not prove the uniform integral theorem.
